items.title: Sub-Part 24: The Mind That Has Travelled Far, Alone, Bodiless, Asleep in a Cave

items.zh: 心遠行、獨行、無身、寐於窟；能調伏難伏，我說婆羅門。
items.en: The mind travels far, travels alone, has no body, and lies dormant in its cave — whoever tames this mind, so hard to tame, that one I call a brahmin.

items.zh: 今此頌中，所言心者，亦名為意，亦名為識。此於過去一切愚夫，無量差別自體展轉及因展轉，雖無作者而流生死，前際叵知，故名遠行。此於現在一一而轉，第二伴心所遠離故，一切種心不頓轉故，名為獨行。又此現在，隨其自體初起現前，或由貪性、或由瞋性、或由癡性、或由一一所餘煩惱隨煩惱性，即彼自體不畢竟轉。如五色根，或同、或異、或劣、或勝，隨其自體初起現前，即此自體畢竟而轉。心不如是。何以故？心經彼彼日夜、剎那、臘縛等位，非一眾多種種品類，異生時生，異滅時滅。由心自性染污之體不成實故，名為無身。此未來世居四識住而有隨眠，可於後生有往來義，名寐於窟。若有聰慧，由此四相，能於過、現、未來世心，如實了知，修厭離滅及心解脫；彼能超度諸薩迦耶，到於彼岸，安住陸地，名婆羅門。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，心於過去長時染污，無作者性；於現在世性是剎那，自性清淨；於未來世由有放逸、不放逸故，染污、清淨。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, 'mind' is also called mentation and also called consciousness. In the past of all fools, it has flowed on in birth-and-death through countless different successions of its own nature and successions of causes, even though there is no agent, and its beginning cannot be known; therefore it is called 'travelling far'. In the present it occurs one at a time, because it is without any second companion mind and because minds of every kind do not occur all at once; therefore it is called 'travelling alone'. Again, in the present, when its own nature first arises and appears, it may be of the nature of greed, of anger, of delusion, or of any one of the remaining afflictions and secondary afflictions; yet that same nature does not continue to the end. The five physical sense faculties, whether the same or different, inferior or superior, once their own nature first arises and appears, continue in that same nature to the end. The mind is not like this. Why? The mind passes through days and nights, moments, lavas and other periods; it is not one but of many various kinds; it arises at different times of arising and ceases at different times of ceasing. Because the defiled substance of the mind's own nature is not real, it is called 'having no body'. In the future it dwells in the four stations of consciousness together with latent tendencies, so that in later lives it can come and go; this is called 'lying dormant in its cave'. If someone wise, through these four aspects, truly knows the mind of the past, present and future, and cultivates disenchantment, dispassion, cessation and liberation of mind, they are able to pass beyond the whole of the existing body (satkāya), reach the other shore and stand on dry land; they are called a brahmin. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows that in the past the mind has been defiled for a long time and is without an agent; that in the present its nature is momentary and its own nature is pure; and that in the future, through heedlessness or heedfulness, it becomes defiled or purified. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 25: Five Questions From Maitreya — What Covers the World, and What Finally Ends It

items.zh: 誰能覆世間？誰能令不顯？誰復能塗染？誰為大怖畏？無明覆世間；放逸令不顯；戲論能塗染；苦為大怖畏。
items.en: What covers the world? What keeps it from shining forth? What further stains it? What is the great terror? Ignorance covers the world; heedlessness keeps it from shining forth; idle speculation stains it; suffering is the great terror.

items.zh: 諸流處處漏，是漏誰能止？當說誰防護？眾流誰所偃？世間諸流漏，是漏念能止。我說能防護，由慧故能偃。
items.en: The floods leak out everywhere — who can stop this leaking? Tell us who provides the guarding, and by whom are the floods dammed? The world's floods leak; mindfulness stops this leaking. I say the guarding comes through this, and it is by wisdom that they are truly dammed.

items.title: Sub-Part 25 Continues: What Finally Ceases, and the Trainee's Graduated Path

items.zh: 念慧與名色，今問是一切，何當永滅盡？唯願為我說。念慧與名色，我說是一切，若諸識永滅，於斯永滅盡。
items.en: Mindfulness, wisdom, and name-and-form — I ask about this whole — when does it finally, completely cease? Please explain this to me. Mindfulness, wisdom, and name-and-form — this I say is the whole — when consciousness itself finally ceases, all of this ceases completely.

items.zh: 云何念所行，諸識當永滅？今請垂方便，為釋令無疑。於內外諸受，都不生欣樂；如是念所行，諸識當永滅。
items.en: In what course of mindfulness does consciousness finally cease? Please, out of compassion, explain this and remove our doubt. Taking no delight in any feeling, inner or outer — this is the course of mindfulness in which consciousness finally ceases.

items.zh: 若諸善說法，及有學異類，彼常委能趣，請大仙為說。不耽著諸欲，其心無濁染，於諸法巧念，是苾芻能趣。此是波羅延中，因阿氏多所請問頌。言世間者，略有三種。一、欲世間，二、色世間，三、無色世間。今此義中，意辨出家、在家二種世間。出家世間復有二種。一、惡說法，二、善說法。惡說法者，無明所覆。善說法者，由有明故，應可顯了；由放逸故，令不顯了。若諸在家異類白衣，為諸戲論之所塗染。當知戲論略有三種。謂三種言事，名為戲論；於四種言說，有所宣談，亦名戲論；能發語言所有尋伺，亦名戲論。若於過去、未來、現在三種言事，依四言說發起異類分別思惟，或違或順，是名塗染。若前戲論，若後塗染，諸在家者多分可得，是故說彼為諸戲論之所塗染。此中惡說法者無明所覆，善說法者放逸不顯，諸在家者戲論塗染，彼於現法苦因轉時，於此苦因不能如實知是苦因；於此苦因愛樂而住。由此因緣，生當來苦，即說此苦名大怖畏。又惡說法者，由無明門，從六處流漏泄眾苦；諸在家者，由戲論門，從六處流漏泄眾苦；善說法者，由放逸門，從六處流漏泄眾苦。如是無明、放逸、戲論諸門流漏，由聞他音、內正作意，於諸行中了知過患；此相應念逆流而轉，故能遮止。如是方便，名伏對治。若出世間正見所攝諸無漏慧，於三種流皆能偃塞。如是方便，名斷對治。於此流漏，若伏、若永二種對治，皆能斷故，俱名防護。又惡說法者及在家者，一向墮於染污品攝。若善說法毘奈耶中，二種可得。諸縱逸者，墮雜染品，非顯了攝；不縱逸者，墮清淨品，顯了所攝。又若已顯了、若應顯了，當知二種皆無放逸。諸阿羅漢斯已顯了，於不放逸，無更須作不放逸事；於四念住，若念若慧已善修故，已善證得清淨識故，唯有決定。於無餘依涅槃界中，善清淨識當永滅故，若念若慧亦隨永滅。餘依所攝先業所引一切名色，亦隨滅盡。乃至彼法未永滅來，於六恒住常善安住；於離欲地所有內受，及於諸欲相應外受，不生欣樂。如是名為諸阿羅漢正念現行，乃至壽盡識方永滅。若諸有學斯應顯了，於不放逸，應更須作不放逸事。彼復二種於不放逸不放逸事，謂常所作、委悉所作。有學異類。若諸有學極七反有，或復家家、一來果等，及於現法堪般涅槃，於下分結及上分結心無染污；為斷彼故，修習對治。又於諸欲不耽著故，諸下分結不能染污。心無濁故，諸上分結不能染污。又於一切有苦法中，如實知集乃至出離，於四念住善住其心。修習如先所得聖道，能趣究竟。如是修習對治道故，彼於一切不放逸中，諸所應作不放逸事，皆得究竟。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，諸在家者及於外法而出家者，決定雜染；及顯於善說法毘奈耶中而出家者，若行放逸墮染污品，若不放逸墮清淨品。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: Those of the well-proclaimed Dharma, and the different kinds of those in training: please, great sage, tell us how they can constantly and thoroughly proceed. Not clinging to sense desires, the mind without turbidity or defilement, skilfully mindful of all things: this is how a monk can proceed. This is a verse asked by Ajita in the Pārāyaṇa. 'The world' is in brief of three kinds: first, the world of desire; second, the world of form; third, the formless world. In the present meaning, the intention is to distinguish two kinds of world: those gone forth and householders. The world of those gone forth is again of two kinds: first, the badly proclaimed Dharma; second, the well-proclaimed Dharma. The badly proclaimed Dharma is covered by ignorance. The well-proclaimed Dharma, because it has understanding, ought to shine forth; because of heedlessness, it is kept from shining forth. Householders, white-robed laypeople of other kinds, are stained by idle speculation. It should be understood that idle speculation is in brief of three kinds: the three topics of speech are called idle speculation; whatever is said in the four kinds of verbal expression is also called idle speculation; and the applied and sustained thought that can give rise to speech is also called idle speculation. When, with regard to the three topics of speech, past, future and present, relying on the four kinds of verbal expression, one gives rise to various kinds of discrimination and thought, whether opposing or agreeing, this is called staining. Both the former, idle speculation, and the latter, staining, are mostly found among householders; therefore they are said to be stained by idle speculation. Among these, those of the badly proclaimed Dharma are covered by ignorance, those of the well-proclaimed Dharma fail to shine forth through heedlessness, and householders are stained by idle speculation. When the cause of suffering is operating here and now, they cannot truly know this cause of suffering as a cause of suffering, and they abide delighting in it. For this reason future suffering arises, and this suffering is called the great terror. Again, those of the badly proclaimed Dharma, through the gate of ignorance, leak out the many sufferings from the streams of the six sense bases; householders, through the gate of idle speculation, leak out the many sufferings from the streams of the six sense bases; those of the well-proclaimed Dharma, through the gate of heedlessness, leak out the many sufferings from the streams of the six sense bases. These leaking streams at the gates of ignorance, heedlessness and idle speculation can be checked because, through hearing another's voice and through inner proper attention, one understands the danger in all formations, and the mindfulness connected with this runs against the stream. This method is called the antidote of suppression. The untainted wisdom included in supramundane right view is able to dam all three streams. This method is called the antidote of abandonment. Because both antidotes against these leaking streams, the suppressing and the permanent, are able to cut them off, both are called guarding. Again, those of the badly proclaimed Dharma and householders fall entirely within the defiled class. In the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya both are found: those who are heedless fall within the defiled class and are not counted among those who shine forth; those who are not heedless fall within the pure class and are counted among those who shine forth. Again, it should be understood that both those who already shine forth and those who ought to shine forth are without heedlessness. Arhats already shine forth; with regard to heedfulness, there is no further work of heedfulness for them to do. Because they have already cultivated well the mindfulness and wisdom of the four foundations of mindfulness, and have already well realised purified consciousness, there is only certainty. Because in the nirvana-element without remainder the well-purified consciousness will cease for ever, mindfulness and wisdom also cease for ever along with it. All name-and-form included in the remainder of the basis and projected by past karma also ceases completely along with it. Until those things have ceased for ever, they constantly abide well in the six constant abidings; and towards the inner feelings of the stages free from desire, and towards the outer feelings connected with sense desires, they take no delight. This is called the operation of right mindfulness in arhats, until consciousness finally ceases at the end of life. Those in training ought to shine forth; with regard to heedfulness, they still need to do the work of heedfulness. For them the work of heedfulness within heedfulness is again of two kinds: what is done constantly and what is done thoroughly. As for the different kinds of those in training: those in training who have at most seven more existences, or who go from family to family, or who have the fruit of once-returning and so on, as well as those able to attain final nirvana here and now, keep their minds undefiled by the lower fetters and the higher fetters; in order to cut these off, they cultivate the antidotes. Again, because they do not cling to sense desires, the lower fetters cannot defile them. Because their mind is without turbidity, the higher fetters cannot defile them. Again, with regard to all phenomena of existence that are suffering, they truly know their origin, and so on up to the escape from them, and settle their minds well in the four foundations of mindfulness. Cultivating the noble path as they had previously attained it, they are able to proceed to the ultimate. Because they cultivate the path of antidotes in this way, they bring to completion all the work of heedfulness that is to be done within heedfulness. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows that householders and those who go forth in outside teachings are certainly defiled; and shows that among those who go forth in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, those who are heedless fall into the defiled class and those who are heedful fall into the pure class. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

blocks.text: A verse on the mind, then a series of questions put to the Buddha by Ajita, from the *Pārāyaṇa* ("Way to the Far Shore") collection. Ru-Yi translates the verses; **the explanations are missing from Ru-Yi's translation**, and the English column gives our own translation.
"The mind travels far, travels alone, has no body, and lies dormant in its cave: whoever tames this mind, so hard to tame, I call a brahmin."

The prose (our translation): - **Travels far:** in the past, without any agent, mind has flowed through countless lives whose beginning cannot be known. - **Travels alone:** in the present it arises one moment at a time; Master Cháng Bǎi: two mental consciousnesses never arise together. - **Has no body:** when a mind arises with greed, hatred, or delusion, that quality does not stay with it as the sense faculties stay what they are. Mind passes through days, moments, instants, ever changing; its defiled nature is not real. Venerable Miào Jìng: "bodiless" means it has no real nature. - **Asleep in a cave:** in the future, it rests in the four abodes of consciousness with its latent tendencies, ready to go on to future lives. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds lie hidden in the ālayavijñāna.
In brief: mind was defiled in the past without any agent; in the present it is momentary and pure in nature; in the future it will be defiled or pure according to heedlessness or heedfulness.

What covers the world? "Ignorance." What keeps it from shining? "Heedlessness." What stains it? "Idle speculation." What is the great terror? "Suffering." Who stops the floods' leaking? "Mindfulness"; and "by wisdom they are dammed".

"The world" here means renunciants and householders. Those under wrong teachings are **covered by ignorance**; those under the good teaching who are heedless **do not shine**; householders are **stained by speculation**: talk about past, present, and future, and the thoughts that drive it. All three, not seeing the cause of suffering as such, enjoy it, and so produce future suffering: "the great terror".

Through the six senses, suffering "leaks". **Mindfulness**, born from hearing and correct attention, runs against the stream and suppresses it; **uncontaminated wisdom** dams it for good. Master Cháng Bǎi: mindfulness subdues; wisdom severs.

For the arhat, at final nirvāṇa without remainder, purified consciousness ceases, and with it mindfulness, wisdom, and all name-and-form. Until then, the arhat takes no delight in any feeling, inner or outer. Trainees, from those with at most seven more lives up to those about to attain nirvāṇa, still have the work of heedfulness to do, constantly and thoroughly: not clinging to desires keeps the lower fetters from staining them, a mind without turbidity keeps the higher fetters away, and so they reach the end. In brief: householders and those gone forth under other teachings are defiled; among the Buddha's renunciants, the heedless fall on the defiled side and the heedful on the pure side.

quiz.q: How does the twenty-fourth verse describe the mind, and who is the brahmin?
options: the mind is a mirror; who keeps it clean is a brahmin
the mind travels far, alone, bodiless, asleep in a cave; whoever tames this hard-to-tame mind I call a brahmin
the mind is a monkey; one born a brahmin is a brahmin
the mind is water; the ritualist is a brahmin
quiz.why: "The mind travels far, travels alone, has no body, and lies dormant in its cave — whoever tames this mind, so hard to tame, that one I call a brahmin." Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the brahmin in the ultimate sense.

quiz.q: How do the two masters relate "travels far, alone, bodiless, asleep in a cave" to the three times?
options: Cháng Bǎi: far-travelling is the past mind, alone and bodiless the present, asleep in a cave the future; Miào Jìng: far-travelling refers to the past mind grasping countless objects
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the past mind is described as travelling far; the present single thought is alone and bodiless; the future mind lies asleep in its cave. Venerable Miào Jìng: in the past our minds grasped at countless objects — that is "the mind travels far."

quiz.q: Why is the mind said to "travel alone," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: when consciousness arises, the prior moment ceases before the next arises — two mental consciousnesses never arise together
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when mental consciousness arises it always goes alone — the prior thought ceases and only then does the next arise; two mental consciousnesses never arise at once, hence "alone." Venerable Miào Jìng: it has no second mind for a companion.

quiz.q: What does "asleep in a cave" stand for, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the seeds of future afflictions lie stored in the ālaya consciousness, like someone asleep in a cave
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of beings' future afflictions are all impressed and hidden in the ālaya consciousness, like a person sleeping in a cave. Venerable Miào Jìng: "asleep" — once awake, it is no longer a seed but a manifest activity.

quiz.q: In answering the four questions, what does the Buddha say covers the world, keeps it from shining, stains it, and is the great terror?
options: ignorance covers, heedlessness keeps it from shining, idle speculation stains, suffering is the great terror
quiz.why: The answer verse: ignorance covers the world; heedlessness keeps it from shining forth; idle speculation stains it; suffering is the great terror.

quiz.q: Second exchange: the floods leak everywhere — what stops them, what guards, and by what are they dammed?
options: the Buddha stops, the Dharma dams
mindfulness stops the leaking; this provides the guarding; it is by wisdom that they are dammed
quiz.why: "The world's floods leak; mindfulness stops this leaking. I say the guarding comes through this, and it is by wisdom that they are truly dammed." Master Cháng Bǎi: the floods are torrents — greed, hatred, and delusion leaking out through the six faculties.

quiz.q: When, according to the Buddha, do mindfulness, wisdom, and name-and-form completely cease?
options: when consciousness itself finally ceases, all of this ceases completely
quiz.why: "Mindfulness, wisdom, and name-and-form — this I say is the whole — when consciousness itself finally ceases, all of this ceases completely." Master Cháng Bǎi: when an arhat enters nirvāṇa without remainder, even the single wholesome thought ceases.
